Question 1
?

The position x of a particle at time t is given by x(t)=t2(2t+4). Calculate the velocity at time t=2.

a
v=38
b
v=22
c
v=14
d
v=32
e
v=40
Submit

decision.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of position. Since x(t)=2t^3+4t^2, v(t)=6t^2+8t, so v(2)=24+16=40.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)={t}^{2}(2t+4).$ Calculate the velocity at time $t=2.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[{t}^{2}(2t+4)] \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}) \\  & =6{t}^{2}+8t\end{aligned}
$$

 

To calculate the velocity at $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =6(2)^{2}+8(2) \\  & =24+16 \\  & =40\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

The position s(t) of a particle (in centimeters) at time t seconds is given by s(t)=5t−10t,t>0. Calculate the speed of the particle when t=2s.

a
1.5cm/s
b
4.0cm/s
c
2.5cm/s
d
2.0cm/s
e
3.0cm/s
Submit

decision.explanation: Rewrite s(t)=5-10/t. Its derivative is v(t)=10/t^2, so the speed at t=2 is |v(2)|=10/4=2.5 cm/s.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in centimeters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=\frac{5t-10}{t},\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{5t-10}{t}) \\  & =\frac{10}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=2,$ the velocity is

$$
v(2)=\frac{10}{(2)^{2}}=\frac{10}{4}=2.5.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|2.5|=2.5\,\text{cm/s}.$

a

b
4.0cm/s
c
2.5cm/s
d
2.0cm/s
e
3.0cm/s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function: v(t)=dsdt=ddt(5t−10t)=10t2

When t=2, the velocity is v(2)=10(2)2=104=2.5. Therefore, the speed is |2.5|=2.5cm/s.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
content.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in centimeters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=\frac{5t-10}{t},\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{5t-10}{t}) \\  & =\frac{10}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=2,$ the velocity is

$$
v(2)=\frac{10}{(2)^{2}}=\frac{10}{4}=2.5.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|2.5|=2.5\,\text{cm/s}.$

$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=1.$

$v(1)=$

after.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(16\sqrt{t}-{t}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{16}{2\sqrt{t}}-4{t}^{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{t}}-4{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1}}-4({1}^{3}) \\  & =8-4 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
